summary.title: Site Reliability Engineering
summary.one_liner: Google's SRE team explains the principles and practices they use to keep very large systems scalable, reliable, and efficient, and how those practices have changed over the decade since the first edition.
keywords: how does google keep systems reliable
takeaways: Google's current SRE practices and how they evolved over the decade since the first edition
Principles for making very large systems scalable, reliable, and efficient
Updated coverage of the value of reliability, cloud reliability, and the impact of AI
Lessons the authors say apply directly to other organizations
summary.summary: This is the landing page for Google's completely rewritten Site Reliability Engineering book, edited by Betsy Beyer, Chris Jones, Christof Leng, David Huska, Jennifer Petoff, and Niall Richard Murphy. The page text describes the book as a revision written by key members of Google's SRE team, documenting how the company's SRE practices have evolved in the decade since the initial publication. It names new topics: the value of reliability, cloud reliability, and the impact of AI. The page text is brief and does not list chapters or detailed contents, so the specifics beyond these points are unknown.
